## Natural history notes

A medium-sized owlet moth characterized by tan to brownish wings with wavy lines and a dry, withered-leaf appearance that helps it blend into dead grasses and leaf litter. In Florida, it is found in grassy open habitats such as prairies, marsh edges, roadsides, fields, lawns, pine flatwoods, and other areas where grasses are abundant. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on grasses and help move grass biomass into the broader food web for birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
